questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The cooperation between Copenhagen University and Charles University in Prague.
Unfortunately, the flow of interaction between the two universities and the cooperation was limited; I experienced too many obstacles and difficulties in the application process, in the flow of information before and during the stay, and in the approval of courses. 
This is especially in the case of Copenhagen University.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Difficult. Not a lack of information but more of a non-streamlined information flow from different actors. Easy to lose oversight.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Online Zoom meeting and three Erasmus coordinators from the university. Really helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They had many nice ice-breaking activities and events in the first week.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dormitory.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A canteen, but it was almost closed at all hours during the day. Really bad food.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's awful. The dormitories were so bad. Really old, dirty, noisy. The only way for me to focus on my studies was to move out, which I did.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If I could choose 0, I would have done that.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was hectic. They opened for registration in September at 11 o, clock. Many of the courses we had approved by Copenhagen University from home were not available at Charles University this semester. So, we applied for all the courses we thought could get approved. The available spaces at many of the few courses we had approved from home were filled up within 2 minutes -  many of us ended up on the waiting list for these courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could write the professors email and explain our situation, they were really helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I got registered in the ones I had approved from home after some days on the waiting lists. 
I had to find other courses as a substitute for the courses which were not available.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that the host university actually provides the cources you got pre-approved.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were pretty low but interesting. Much more participation, which was good for the learning outcome. The syllabus didn't always match what was taught in class. We didn't even have to read or use the texts.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Copenhagen University is at a much higher level.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Democracy - Current Challenges and Innovation.
EU Comparative politics: tension in representative democracy.
Ethnic Issues and Territories in Eastern, East Central and Southeastern Europe.
Introduction to the theories on EU integration.
Media in Foreign Policy.
Energy Security in Israel and the Middle East.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Media in Foreign Policy.
Energy Security in Israel and the Middle East.

These courses were really interesting. Empirical interesting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had many nice What's-app groups offering almost everything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: They had many nice What's-app groups offering almost everything.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Do weekend trips to Brno, Vienna (Austria), and Krakow (Poland). 
Go hiking. 
Go partying.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Takes some time and energy, but mostly in the beginning 4 weeks.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in the events arranged by the university.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Czechs are not as friendly-minded as Danes. But this is often only at the first eye-cast.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The beer culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The culture and the thing about living in an other country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The approval of courses by Copenhagen University.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
